method_md:
# waterhammer.html: method specification for an independent reference

Scope: the hydraulic model behind `waterhammer.html` (manifest revision `2026-10-16.waterhammer-4`; the changes against `2026-09-10.report-profile-1` are listed in §12 and §13) as far as the cases in `cases.json` use it: single elastic pipe, upstream reservoir with optional quadratic pump and check valve, downstream orifice valve to a tailwater level, quasi-steady and unsteady friction, linear or piecewise-linear elevation, classical DVCM and threshold cavitation, and the wave-speed relations of the axial-FSI branch. Surge vessel, air valve, viscoelastic wall, Suter 4Q pump and the FSI transient are switched off in every case and are not specified here.

The page's own Learn text and manifest are quoted where they state a law. Where they are silent, the law the code applies is written out as an equation and marked **(code)**.

## 1. Inputs and units

Every case stores the complete tool state as `input.controls`, a case file of schema `tools.petrov.re/waterhammer-case/v1`. Values are strings exactly as the page serialises them; parse each with `Number()`. Booleans are JSON booleans. `N` is rounded to the nearest integer (`Math.round`).

| control | unit on page | conversion to SI used by the solver | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| L | m | – | pipe length |
| D | m | – | inside diameter; A = πD²/4 |
| eps | mm | ε = eps/1000 m | roughness |
| a | m/s | – | wave speed (user input; not derived from material data) |
| z0, z1 | m | – | end elevations (linear mode) |
| elevMode | `linear` / `profile` | – | geometry mode |
| elevData | text | – | profile rows `x,z` (m chainage, m elevation), one per line |
| rho | kg/m³ | – | liquid density ρ |
| nu | m²/s | – | kinematic viscosity ν |
| patm | kPa abs | ×1000 Pa | atmospheric pressure |
| pvap | kPa abs | ×1000 Pa | vapour pressure |
| cavModel | `dvcm` / `threshold` | – | cavitation model |
| dvcmPsi | – | – | DVCM weighting ψ |
| Q0 | m³/s | – | initial flow |
| frictionModel | `quasi`, `zielke`, `universal`, `vardy`, `vardyRough` | – | friction model |
| Hres | m | – | upstream (suction) reservoir head |
| Htail | m | – | tailwater head downstream of the valve |
| pumpOn, pumpModel | bool, `simple` | – | quadratic pump in service |
| pumpH0 | m | – | shut-off head H₀ |
| pumpQr, pumpHr | m³/s, m | – | reference flow and head |
| valveEvent | bool | – | valve manoeuvre enabled |
| valveStart | s | – | start of travel t_s |
| valveClose | s | – | travel duration t_c |
| valveFinal | % | τ_f = valveFinal/100 | final relative opening |
| valveLaw | `linear`, `cosine`, `power` | – | travel law |
| valveExp | – | – | exponent m of the power law |
| pumpTrip, tripTime, coastTau | bool, s, s | – | pump trip and coast-down constant |
| checkMode | `auto`, `none`, `ideal`, `dynamic` | – | check valve at the pump/reservoir outlet; `auto` (default) resolves to `ideal` if pumpOn, else `none` (§6.1) |
| checkTrigger, checkDelay, checkClose, checkLaw, checkDp | `trip`, s, s, `cosine`/`linear`, m | – | dynamic check valve |
| N | – | integer | number of reaches |
| T | s | – | requested duration |
| fsiOn, fsiBulk, fsiThickness, fsiE, fsiPoisson, fsiRhoS | bool, GPa, mm, GPa, –, kg/m³ | K = ×1e9 Pa, e = /1000 m, E = ×1e9 Pa | axial FSI branch (wave-speed cases only) |

Constants: g = 9.80665 m/s². Gauge pressure in bar: p = ρg(H − z)/10⁵. Absolute pressure: p_abs = patm + ρg(H − z).

## 2. Wave speed and pipe restraint

Standard hydraulic model: the wave speed is the input `a`. The page states: "Wave speed a is a user input for the standard hydraulic model; it is not derived from pipe material data. Only the optional axial-FSI branch computes wave speed." No restraint factor is applied in the standard model.

Axial FSI branch (Learn text, Tijsseling 2003), used only by the `wave_speed` cases. With R = D/2 (inner radius), wall thickness e, Young modulus E, Poisson ratio ν, pipe density ρ_s, fluid bulk modulus K:

- c_f² = [ρ/K + (1 − ν²)·2ρR/(E e)]⁻¹ (classical fluid wave speed; the factor 1 − ν² is the restraint factor of a pipe anchored against axial movement, Wylie & Streeter c₁ = 1 − ν²)
- c_s² = E/ρ_s
- γ² = [1 + 2ν²(ρ/ρ_s)(R/e)]·c_f² + c_s² **(code)**
- λ⁴ − γ²λ² + c_f²c_s² = 0, so λ₁,₃² = ½[γ² ∓ √(γ⁴ − 4c_f²c_s²)], λ₁ < λ₃.
- FSI grid: dx = L/N, dt = dx/λ₃, steps = floor(T/dt + 1e-10).

FSI input guards (all refuse): pump on or trip; checkMode ≠ none; surge or air device on; cavModel ≠ threshold; friction ≠ quasi or |ε| > 1e-15; elevMode ≠ linear or z₀ ≠ z₁; e ≥ D/4; ν ∉ [0, 0.5); N outside 16…220; Hres ≤ Htail unless the closure is instantaneous at t = 0 to zero; steps < 1 or > 30000. FSI status (revision 2026-10-16) is `warn` only when a stated condition fires. The slow wave family moves σ = λ₁/λ₃ reaches per step and is found by linear interpolation between nodes. For a Fourier mode with phase step θ per reach, the interpolation amplifies it by |G|² = 1 − 2σ(1 − σ)(1 − cos θ). The check uses the fundamental fluid-dominated mode, wavelength 4L (reservoir to closed valve), so θ = π/(2N). The predicted amplitude loss over the run is ℓ = 1 − |G|^steps, exported as `slowModeInterpolationLoss`. The run warns when ℓ > 0.01 ("Slow FSI wave family: linear characteristic interpolation (Courant …) is predicted to damp the fundamental mode (wavelength 4L) by …% over the run (limit 1%) …"). The other FSI warnings are a thick wall (e/D > 0.10) and the vapour threshold being crossed.

## 3. Grid

- dx = L/N, dt = dx/a (Courant number exactly 1). L and a are **not** adjusted.
- steps = floor(T/dt + 1e-10); simulated end Tsim = steps·dt; time level n is at t_n = n·dt (computed as the product, not by accumulation).
- Nodes j = 0…N at x_j = j·dx. Node 0 is the upstream boundary (reservoir/pump), node N the upstream face of the outlet valve.
- Elevation at nodes: linear mode z_j = z₀ + (z₁ − z₀)·x_j/L. Profile mode: piecewise-linear interpolation of the profile points at x_j (Learn: "Profile mode linearly interpolates user x,z points onto the MOC grid").

## 4. Steady state (t = 0)

- V₀ = Q₀/A, Re₀ = V₀D/ν.
- Darcy friction factor f(Re, ε/D) (Learn: "f=64/Re below Re=2000, iterative Colebrook–White above Re=4000, and a smooth numerical bridge over Re=2000…4000"). Exact law **(code)**:
  - Re ≤ 0: f = 0.
  - Re < 2000: f = 64/Re.
  - Re ≥ 4000: f = f_CW(Re, ε/D).
  - 2000 ≤ Re < 4000: t = (Re − 2000)/2000, s = t²(3 − 2t), f = (64/Re)(1 − s) + f_CW(Re, ε/D)·s.
  - f_CW: root of 1/√f = −2 log₁₀(ε/(3.7D) + 2.51/(Re√f)). The page starts from Swamee–Jain f₀ = 0.25/[log₁₀(ε/(3.7D) + 5.74/Re^0.9)]² and applies 3 Newton steps on x = 1/√f; this is converged to round-off (relative 1e-15) over the whole Re/ε range, so any converged Colebrook root is equivalent.
- Friction loss hf = f·(L/D)·V₀²/(2g).
- Pump head at Q₀ (if pumpOn, quadratic): H_p(Q₀) = H₀ − kQ₀|Q₀| with k = (H₀ − H_r)/Q_r²; 0 if no pump.
- Head at node 0: H_up = Hres + H_p(Q₀) − (checkDp if checkMode = dynamic, else 0).
- Head at the valve: H_end = H_up − hf. Valve head drop ΔH_v = H_end − Htail; refused if ΔH_v ≤ 1e-6 m.
- Valve coefficient k_v = Q₀/√ΔH_v.
- Initial field: H_j = H_up − hf·j/N, Q_j = Q₀ on both sides of every node (the initial HGL is linear in chainage in both elevation modes).
- Initial single-phase check: refused if p_abs ≤ pvap at any node, and in profile mode also at any profile vertex evaluated with the linear HGL at that vertex's x.

## 5. Compatibility equations (interior)

Learn: C⁺ = H + BQ − RQ|Q| − J_u, C⁻ = H − BQ + RQ|Q| + J_u, B = a/(gA). With known values at time level n−1 (superscript omitted):

- C_P(j) = H_{j−1} + B·Q^R_{j−1} − R(Q^R_{j−1})·Q^R_{j−1}|Q^R_{j−1}| − J_u^R(j−1)
- C_M(j) = H_{j+1} − B·Q^L_{j+1} + R(Q^L_{j+1})·Q^L_{j+1}|Q^L_{j+1}| + J_u^L(j+1)

where Q^R_j is the flow on the downstream side of node j (start of reach j→j+1) and Q^L_j the flow on its upstream side (end of reach j−1→j); they differ only at a vapour cavity or at node 0 with a cavity. The friction resistance is quasi-steady and explicit at the characteristic foot **(code)**:

R(Q) = f(Re_foot, ε/D)·dx/(2gDA²), Re_foot = |Q|·D/(Aν), using the friction law of §4.

Interior node without cavity: H_j = (C_P + C_M)/2, Q_j = (C_P − C_M)/(2B), Q^L = Q^R = Q_j.

Elevation enters only through z in pressure and in the vapour head h_v(j) = z_j + (pvap − patm)/(ρg); H is piezometric head.

## 6. Boundary conditions

### 6.1 Upstream reservoir / pump (node 0)

Unknown flow q into the pipe; C⁻ gives H₀ = C_M(0) + Bq. Source equation **(code)**:

C_M(0) + Bq = Hres + H_p(q, t) − sgn(q)·h_cv·(q/Q₀)²/A_cv²

- H_p(q, t) = H₀·s(t)² − kq|q| (quadratic pump; 0 if pump off). Speed ratio s(t) = 1 for t ≤ tripTime or no trip, else s = exp[−(t − tripTime)/coastTau] (Learn: n = exp[−(t−t_trip)/τ]).
- check loss term only for checkMode = dynamic: h_cv = checkDp, A_cv = max(c(t), 1e-4) with c(t) the check travel (below); if c(t) < 1e-5 the valve is closed: q = 0, H₀ = C_M(0).
- checkMode = auto is resolved before the run: ideal if pumpOn is true, none otherwise. A loaded state that has no checkMode field is given checkMode = auto.
- checkMode = ideal (set explicitly, or resolved from auto with a pump): if the root q < 0 then q = 0 and H₀ = C_M(0) (dead end). An explicit ideal applies whether or not the pump is on.
- checkMode = none, pump off: q = (Hres − C_M(0))/B, H₀ = Hres.
- Quadratic pump in service and the solved flow q < −1e-8 m³/s: the run is refused ("Reverse flow through the in-service pump begins at t=…").
- Dynamic check travel: t_s = t_trig + checkDelay; c = 1 for t ≤ t_s; else u = clamp((t − t_s)/checkClose, 0, 1), with u ← ½ − ½cos(πu) for checkLaw = cosine (unchanged for linear), and c = 1 − u. The trigger time t_trig is set once and never reset.
  - checkTrigger = trip: t_trig = tripTime.
  - checkTrigger = flow (revision 2026-10-16 clause; describes the page, unchanged since revision -3). At every level n, before the node-0 boundary of that level is solved and while t_trig is still unset:
    1. Solve the node-0 boundary with the check valve forced fully open (c = 1, loss h_cv(q/Q₀)²). This includes the DVCM branch: if V^{n−1}_0 > V_tol, or the open-valve head ≤ h_v(0), the source flow is solved at H₀ = h_v(0). Call the resulting source-side (pump-side) flow q_open^n.
    2. If q_open^n ≤ 0, the trigger fires with an interpolated zero crossing: t_trig = t_{n−1} + φ·dt.
       - φ = q^{n−1}/(q^{n−1} − q_open^n), clamped to [0, 1], when q^{n−1} > 0 and q^{n−1} ≠ q_open^n; otherwise φ = 1.
       - q^{n−1} is the source-side flow actually obtained at level n−1.
    3. Level n itself is then solved with c(t_n) from this t_trig. With checkDelay = 0 the valve has already moved by level n: c(t_n) = 1 − u((t_n − t_trig)/checkClose).
    The trigger therefore uses "≤ 0" on the open-valve candidate flow. It does not use the solved flow of level n, and it does not start the travel at t_n. If it never fires, the run warns ("Flow-reversal check-valve trigger did not occur within the simulated duration."). With a pump in service the flow trigger is refused unless the pump uses Suter 4Q data (§10).

The page solves the scalar source/valve equations with a bracketing root finder started at the previous step's flow; it accepts |residual| < 1e-10 m at the start point or bisects to |residual| < 1e-11 m (max 70 bisections), and picks the root nearest the previous flow. H₀ is then evaluated as C_M(0) + Bq, so it equals Hres only to that residual.

### 6.2 Outlet valve (node N) to tailwater

Relative opening τ(t) (Learn: "an ideal orifice. Its coefficient is inferred from the initial operating point, then multiplied by the commanded opening"):

- t ≤ t_s or valveEvent off: τ = 1.
- t_c ≤ 1e-9 (instantaneous): τ = τ_f for t > t_s.
- else u = clamp((t − t_s)/t_c, 0, 1); linear: u; cosine: u ← ½ − ½cos(πu); power: u ← u^m; τ = 1 − (1 − τ_f)·u.

Closure therefore first acts at the first time level with t > t_s (strict).

Valve equation: C_P(N) − Bq − Htail = sgn(q)·(q/C_v)², C_v = k_v·τ(t); H_N = C_P(N) − Bq. If τ < 1e-6: q = 0, H_N = C_P(N) (dead end).

## 7. Cavitation

### 7.1 Threshold model
No cavity is formed; the single-phase solution continues. After each level (including n = 0), nodes with p_abs ≤ pvap are counted; the first one (earliest level, lowest node) is reported and the status becomes `warn` ("vapor pressure reached at x=…, t=…").

### 7.2 Classical DVCM (Learn: "a node that reaches vapor pressure is held at P_vap while separate upstream/downstream characteristic flows grow or collapse a discrete vapor cavity using dV_cav/dt = Q_out − Q_in … ψ weights the current imbalance against the value two MOC steps earlier")

Cavity tolerance V_tol = max(1e-12, A·dx·1e-12). At step n, per node, V^{n−1} (previous), V^{n−2} and ΔQ^{n−2} (the imbalance recorded at that node two steps earlier; 0 if the cavity routine did not run there at that step) are known. The cavity routine **(code)**:

ΔQ^n = Q_out − Q_in; V^n = V^{n−2} + 2dt·[ψΔQ^n + (1 − ψ)ΔQ^{n−2}].
If V^n > V_tol the cavity is active, else V^n = 0.

Interior node j, entered when V^{n−1}_j > V_tol or (C_P + C_M)/2 ≤ h_v(j):
- H = h_v(j), Q_in = (C_P − h_v)/B, Q_out = (h_v − C_M)/B, run the cavity routine.
- Active: H_j = h_v, Q^L_j = Q_in, Q^R_j = Q_out.
- Not active (collapse step; Bergant, Simpson & Tijsseling 2006; Wylie & Streeter ch. 8): single-phase restart H* = (C_P + C_M)/2.
  - If H* ≥ h_v(j): H_j = H*, Q^L = Q^R = (C_P − C_M)/(2B); both compatibility equations hold.
  - If H* < h_v(j): the node recavitates at this step. H_j = h_v, Q^L = Q_in, Q^R = Q_out (the values above), and a fresh cavity is opened by the fresh-cavity step below.

Node 0 (source), entered when V^{n−1}_0 > V_tol or the normal boundary head ≤ h_v(0): H₀ = h_v(0); Q_in = source flow at that head (source equation of §6.1 solved for q with H₀ given); Q_out = (h_v − C_M(0))/B; cavity routine. Not active: normal boundary solution (H_normal, q_normal). If H_normal ≥ h_v(0): H₀ = H_normal, Q_in = Q_out = q_normal. Otherwise the node recavitates: H₀ = h_v(0), Q_in and Q_out are the values at h_v given above, and the fresh-cavity step runs.

Node N (valve), entered when V^{n−1}_N > V_tol or the normal valve head ≤ h_v(N): Q_in = (C_P(N) − h_v)/B; Q_out = sgn(h_v − Htail)·C_v√|h_v − Htail| (0 if τ < 1e-6); cavity routine. Active: H_N = h_v. Not active: normal valve solution (H_normal, q_normal). If H_normal ≥ h_v(N): H_N = H_normal, Q_in = Q_out = q_normal. Otherwise the node recavitates: H_N = h_v, Q_in and Q_out are the values at h_v given above, and the fresh-cavity step runs.

Fresh-cavity step (revision 2026-10-15): ΔQ^n = Q_out − Q_in at h_v; V^n = 2dt·ψ·ΔQ^n, i.e. the ψ-weighted update with V^{n−2} = 0 and no history term. ΔQ^n is recorded for use two steps later. If V^n > V_tol the cavity is active and counts as an opening (and a growth event); otherwise V^n = 0 while H stays at h_v with the flows at h_v. With H* < h_v, ΔQ^n = 2(h_v − H*)/B > 0 at an interior node, so the new cavity is always active there.

Node order within a step: node 0, interior nodes j = 1…N−1 ascending, node N. Cavity statistics: openings (V^{n−1} ≤ V_tol → V^n > V_tol), collapses (V^{n−1} > V_tol and routine yields inactive), the first growth event, the maximum volume (strictly greater comparison in evaluation order) and the ratio V/(A·dx·w), w = ½ at j = 0, N, else 1. Wave speed is unchanged by cavities.

## 8. Unsteady friction

Learn: four convolution modes. All share the recursive form **(code)**:

- Dimensionless step Δτ = 4ν·dt/D².
- Each node side (R and L of every node j = 0…N) carries K history states y_k, initially 0.
- Head term J_u = C_u·Σ_k y_k, C_u = 16ν·dt·a/(D²·A·g). J_u^R(j) uses the R states of node j, J_u^L(j) the L states (§5).
- After all nodes of step n are solved, every node side is updated with its own flow change ΔQ = Q^n − Q^{n−1} (Q^R for R states, Q^L for L states): y_k ← e^{−n_kΔτ}·y_k + m_k·e^{−n_kΔτ/2}·ΔQ.
- J_u is signed (no |Q| or sign factor).

Coefficient sets:

**Zielke (laminar)**, K = 26 (Urbanowicz & Zarzycki 2012, 26-term approximation). m_k = ZL_M, n_k = ZL_N:

ZL_M = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2.141, 4.544, 7.566, 11.299, 16.531, 24.794, 36.229, 52.576, 78.150, 113.873, 165.353, 247.915, 369.561, 546.456, 818.871, 1209.771, 1770.756, 2651.257, 3968.686, 5789.566, 8949.468]

ZL_N = [26.3744, 70.8493, 135.0198, 218.9216, 322.5544, 499.148, 1072.543, 2663.013, 6566.001, 15410.459, 35414.779, 80188.189, 177078.960, 388697.936, 850530.325, 1835847.582, 3977177.832, 8721494.927, 19120835.527, 42098544.558, 92940512.285, 203458923.000, 445270063.893, 985067938.878, 2166385706.058, 4766167206.672]

Allowed for 0 < Re₀ ≤ 2000, otherwise refused ("Zielke laminar weighting requires initial Reynolds number at or below 2,000; current Re₀=…").

**Vardy–Brown smooth turbulent (frozen at Re₀)**, K = 16, W(τ) = A*·e^{−B*τ}/√τ represented by m_k = A*·VB_M_k, n_k = VB_N_k + B*:
- A* = 1/(2√π); κ = log₁₀(15.29·Re₀^−0.0567); B* = Re₀^κ/12.86.

VB_M = [5.03362, 6.4876, 10.7735, 19.904, 37.4754, 70.7117, 133.460, 251.933, 476.597, 902.22, 1602.04, 2894.84, 5085.55, 9190.11, 16118.6, 29117.3]

VB_N = [4.78793, 51.0897, 210.868, 765.03, 2731.01, 9731.44, 34668.5, 123511, 440374, 1578229, 5481659, 18255921, 59753474, 192067361, 616415963, 1945566788]

Allowed for 2000 < Re₀ ≤ 1e8 and, when Re₀ ≥ 4000, only for a smooth-dominant wall (§8.1).

**Vardy–Brown fully rough (frozen at Re₀)**: same 16 exponentials, m_k = A*·VB_M_k, n_k = VB_N_k + B*, with A* = 0.0103·√Re₀·(ε/D)^0.39, B* = 0.352·Re₀·(ε/D)^0.41 (manifest/Learn). Allowed for 4000 ≤ Re₀ ≤ 1e8, 1e-6 ≤ ε/D ≤ 1e-2, fully-rough-dominant wall only.

**Universal (Urbanowicz, Zarzycki & Kudźma 2012)**, K = 26: m_k = ZL_M_k (unchanged), n_k = max(1e-12, ZL_N_k + shift), with shift evaluated at every state update from the local Reynolds number of the new flow of that node side, Re = |Q^n|·D/(Aν):
- shift = 0 for Re ≤ 2320;
- shift = B*(Re) − B*(2320) for Re > 2320, where B*(r) = r^κ(r)/12.86, κ(r) = log₁₀(15.29·r^−0.0567).
In the laminar range it is therefore identical to Zielke. Allowed for 0 < Re₀ ≤ 1e8 and, when Re₀ ≥ 4000, smooth-dominant wall only.

Source of this rule (Urbanowicz, Zarzycki & Kudźma 2012, Eq. 3.2; Vardy–Brown scaling after Vitkovsky et al. 2004):
- Before the run, universal coefficients are formed at Re_cr = 2320: m_iu = m_i/A* and n_iu = n_i − B*(Re_cr), with A* = 1/(2√π).
- In turbulent flow the current coefficients are m_i,c = A*·m_iu and n_i,c = n_iu + B*(Re_c). They are updated every step with the current Reynolds number, and the history states are kept across the Re = 2320 switch.
- A* cancels: m_i,c = m_i and n_i,c = n_i + B*(Re_c) − B*(2320), which is the rule above.
- The paper describes Re_c as the current local Reynolds number. The page evaluates it per node side from the new flow; the paper's Fig. 3 scheme was not available as text, so this per-node-side reading is the page's.

### 8.1 Wall-regime guard (Colebrook term dominance)
For Re₀ ≥ 4000 and ε > 0: f = f_CW, rough = (ε/D)/3.7, visc = 2.51/(Re₀√f), roughShare = rough/(rough + visc), χ = visc/rough. Smooth-dominant if roughShare ≤ 0.10, fully-rough-dominant if ≥ 0.90, otherwise transitionally rough. ε = 0 is smooth-dominant.

## 9. Pressure extrema and stored output

After every level n = 0…steps the gauge pressure of every node is compared with the running envelope. The global maximum keeps the first (level, node) at which it is attained; a later value replaces it only when it exceeds the stored one by more than 1e-12·max(1, |p|) (otherwise only the value is updated). Same for the minimum. Display frames are stored every ceil(steps/520) steps plus the last step; in every case graded with node histories or node extrema steps ≤ 520, so every level is stored.

## 10. Refusals and warnings

Refusals (no result; status kind `err`):
- any of L, D, eps, a, z0, z1, rho, nu, patm, pvap, Q0, Hres, Htail, N, T non-finite; any of L, D, a, rho, nu, patm, pvap, Q0, T not positive; pvap ≥ patm; eps < 0;
- ψ outside [0.5, 1];
- checkMode, after `auto` is resolved, not one of none, ideal, dynamic ("Unknown check-valve model. Use auto, none, ideal or dynamic.");
- N < 16 or N > 220 ("Pipe segments must be between 16 and 220.");
- quadratic pump: Q_r, H_r not positive; H₀ < 0; H₀ < H_r;
- valveFinal outside 0–100 %; valveStart < 0; valveClose < 0; valveExp ≤ 0;
- pump trip without pump; trip time < 0; coastTau ≤ 0;
- dynamic check: trip trigger without trip; flow trigger with quadratic pump in service; delay < 0; closure time ≤ 0; checkDp < 0;
- steps < 1 ("Duration must be at least one MOC step (… s)."); steps > 30000;
- inconsistent operating point ΔH_v ≤ 1e-6 m ("Initial operating point is inconsistent: only … m head remains across the outlet valve …");
- profile: fewer than 2 points, endpoints not at 0 and L (tolerance max(1e-7, 1e-8·L)), x outside 0…L;
- initial state at or below vapour pressure at a node or profile vertex;
- friction model applicability (§8);
- runtime: reverse flow through a quadratic pump (§6.1); non-convergent boundary root.

Warnings (solved, status kind `warn`); the status line appends them:
- threshold model reached vapour pressure; any DVCM cavity formed (status always reports the first cavity, max cavity, max cavity/reach ratio, openings, collapses);
- DVCM cavity/reach ratio > 10 %;
- profile vertex (interior only) farther than max(1e-8, 1e-6·dx) from its nearest node round(x/dx);
- event resolution < 10 steps: valve closure t_c/dt (only if t_c > 0), quadratic-pump coastTau/dt (if trip), dynamic check closure time/dt;
- Zielke with Re₀ > 1900;
- Vardy–Brown (smooth or rough): Δτ/2 < 1e-9, Δτ > 0.1, any updated flow Q^R or Q^L < −1e-9 at any node (frozen coefficients through flow reversal); fully rough also χ > 0.10;
- universal: Δτ/2 < 1e-9 or Δτ > 1e-3; maximum local Re > 1e7.

## 11. Ambiguities and points a reference must decide

1. Boundary roots are found numerically to |residual| < 1e-11 m (§6.1). A closed-form reference will differ from the page at that level in heads and about 1e-11/B in flows.
2. Time of an extremum on a plateau: the graded definitions use the first level within 1e-9 m (node extrema) and the page's 1e-12 relative tie rule (global extrema). Near-ties can shift the reported time by whole steps without any change in value.
3. The quasi-steady friction is explicit at the characteristic foot (first order in |Q|Q). A reference using a second-order or implicit friction treatment will not match to round-off.
4. J_u is signed and is accumulated per node side from ΔQ of that side; the R state of node N and the L state of node 0 are updated but never used.
5. Universal mode above Re = 2320 follows Eq. 3.2 of Urbanowicz, Zarzycki & Kudźma (2012), and A* cancels (§8). The remaining reading is which Reynolds number counts as "current local": the page uses |Q^n| of each node side.
6. DVCM collapse step (revised 2026-10-15): no node is ever below h_v. A restart below h_v recavitates the node, and the volume of the collapsed cavity and its imbalance history are discarded (fresh cavity from zero). In the cases the recavitation occurs only at interior nodes. The node 0 and node N branches are implemented with the same rule, but no case reaches them.
7. An explicit checkMode = ideal also acts when no pump is fitted (reverse flow into the reservoir is blocked, node 0 becomes a dead end). The default is `auto` (§6.1). Every case stores checkMode explicitly except `check_migration_missing_field`, which tests the migration rule.
8. Bergant/Adelaide cases: the page uses a smooth-cosine 9 ms closure starting at t = 0 as a surrogate for the recorded valve trace; inputs (ν from Re = 5970, ε = 9e-5·D, Htail = Hres − hf − 0.001 m, pvap from a 10.25 m vapour gauge head, z rising 0 → 2.03 m) are stored as numbers in the case.
9. The initial HGL is linear in chainage in profile mode; it ignores the profile shape.
10. In profile mode, a vertex between nodes is represented only through interpolated nodal z.

## 12. Revision 2026-10-15 (`2026-10-15.waterhammer-3`)

Changes against `2026-09-10.report-profile-1` (and the identical solver of `2026-10-11.waterhammer-bench-2`):

1. Check-valve default (§1, §6.1, ambiguity 7). New model value `auto`, which is the default: `ideal` when a pump is in service, `none` otherwise. A saved state or permalink that names a model keeps it. A state loaded without the checkMode field becomes `auto`.
2. DVCM collapse step (§7.2, ambiguity 6), all nodes. Before: H = max(H*, h_v), with the flow taken from one characteristic only, so one compatibility equation (or, at node N, the valve equation) failed whenever the clamp acted. Now: if H* ≥ h_v, H = H* with the single-phase flow from both characteristics; if H* < h_v, the node recavitates (H = h_v, flows from each characteristic and the boundary equation at h_v, fresh cavity from zero volume). Results differ from before only when H* < h_v at a collapse step.
3. Smooth Vardy–Brown output (§8). The run result now carries A* = 1/(2√π) next to B*. The solver is unchanged.
4. An unrecognised checkMode is refused (§10).
5. Manifest description: one sentence on the `auto` default. Manifest limitations: one sentence on the collapse/restart rule. Both in 7 languages.

The page's python export covers only the quasi-steady core and lists DVCM as out of scope, so it needed no change.

Not changed in revision 2026-10-15: the universal model above Re = 2320 and the FSI mesh notice (both addressed in §13).

## 13. Revision 2026-10-16 (`2026-10-16.waterhammer-4`)

1. Universal unsteady friction (§8, ambiguity 5). The coefficient rule was checked against Eq. 3.2 of Urbanowicz, Zarzycki & Kudźma (2012) and the Vardy–Brown scaling it cites, and the page already applies it: A* cancels and the decay rates shift by B*(Re_c) − B*(2320). The solver is unchanged; the page code now cites the equation.
2. FSI status (§2). The unconditional interpolation notice is replaced by the condition ℓ > 1 % (predicted amplitude loss of the fundamental slow-family mode). Without that condition, a thick wall or a vapour crossing, an FSI run now reports `ok`. The mesh-convergence statement stays in the Learn text and the manifest limitations.
3. Node 0 dead end (§6.1, §7.2). No change. With no pump and a check valve set to ideal or none, the source equation has no flow term. Node 0 is then held at Hres while the valve is open, and stays above Hres when an ideal valve closes, because closing requires C_M(0) > Hres. So node 0 cannot reach h_v(0) < Hres, and the head-given source flow is never requested. Node 0 can reach h_v only behind a closed dynamic check valve (opening < 1e-5). There the source flow is 0 and node 0 is a dead end holding a discrete DVCM cavity (case `node0_deadend_dvcm_dynamic_check`).
4. Flow-triggered dynamic check valve (§6.1). The page's rule was not written down before this revision; it is now. The candidate flow comes from the fully open valve, the trigger condition is ≤ 0, the trigger time is the interpolated zero crossing, and the same level already uses c(t_n). The solver is unchanged.

times t_* and node/step indices.why: times are n*dt on the shared grid; plateau near-ties (1e-9 m / 1e-12 rel) can shift by whole steps (ambiguity 2).

source.*.why: root residual 1e-11 m / B (B ~ 360 s/m2 here) ~ 3e-14; 1e-9 leaves margin for summation order.

unsteady.Ju_max_m.why: sum of 16-26 exponential states; round-off only.

unsteady_re_range.*.why: minRe is |Q| at a near-zero crossing and depends on 1e-11-level flow differences; maxRe is ~Re0.

cavity heads/pressures (DVCM cases).why: DVCM switching (entry when H <= h_v, active when V > V_tol) can flip on 1e-11 differences and shift a collapse by a step; typical DVCM sensitivity in the literature (Bergant & Simpson 1999) is at the mm level once a cavity forms.

cavity.V_max_m3.why: integrated imbalance; inherits DVCM switching sensitivity.

cavity.openings / collapses.why: count of tolerance crossings at V_tol ~ 1e-12 A dx; round-off can add/remove a transient micro-cavity.

threshold_cavitation.first_j/first_t_s.why: p_abs <= pvap test on a sharp head front; if a node sits within 1e-9 m of h_v it may move one step.

concern.text: Checked against Urbanowicz, Zarzycki & Kudzma (2012), JTAM 50(4) 889-902, Eq. (3.2): universal coefficients are formed before the run at Re_cr = 2320 as m_iu = m_i/A* and n_iu = n_i - B*(2320), A* = sqrt(1/(4 pi)); in turbulent flow they are rescaled by the Vitkovsky et al. (2004) procedure (m = A* m_iu, n = n_iu + B*(Re)). A* cancels and the B*(2320) offset is part of the published rule, so the 2026-10-11 remark that the paper has no offset is retracted; method.md section 8 equals Eq. (3.2). Residual reading, not a defect: the paper states the coefficients are updated every step with the current Re (its Fig. 3 scheme gives no formula); method.md takes |Q^n| per node side. Near flow reversal the local Re falls below 2320 and the weights return to Zielke's; a frozen Re0 (Vardy-Brown practice) is the alternative. The effect on graded values is below 0.03 m here.
